subject: Data Engineering
title: ETL vs ELT
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: ETL vs ELT.

hook.text: For decades, data was transformed before loading. Then cloud warehouses flipped the order.

buildup.text: ETL transforms data in a staging area, then loads the clean result into the warehouse.

discovery.text: ELT loads raw data first, then uses the warehouse's own compute power to transform it in place.

twist.text: ELT became dominant because cloud warehouses are so powerful that transforming inside is cheaper.

climax.text: ELT also preserves raw data, letting analysts rewrite transforms without re-extracting.

punchline.text: Load first, ask questions later. That's ELT.

quiz.question: What is the key difference between ETL and ELT?
options: ELT transforms data after loading; ETL transforms before
ELT does not require a warehouse
